chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:

Ammar asked him, while I was with him, about a man who marries the promiscuous woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah). He said, 'There is no harm, and if the other marriage is [permanent], let him guard his door.'

key_terms.الْفَاجِرَة: The promiscuous woman (one known for fornication or sexual indiscretion)
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يُحْصِنْ بَابَهُ: Guard his door (idiom for managing household privacy or keeping the wife separate)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a promiscuous woman for temporary marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chain of Zurarah, this hadith clarifies that temporary marriage (mut'ah) remains valid even with a woman of loose moral character, provided the contractual conditions are met. The Imam’s instruction to 'guard his door' if the man has a permanent wife highlights the practical necessity of maintaining household order and preventing conflict between wives, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of mut'ah within the broader framework of marital ethics.
